Read .rds file 
# Read Saved Data (see load_salary_data.r)
df <- readRDS(file.path(
  dirname(this.path()),
  "..",
  "data",
  "clean",
  "annual_salary_data.rds"
))

Adjust Salaries for Inflaiton:

Account for inflation using the consumer price index with 2024 as the base year.

Code 
yearly_cpi <- data.frame(
  year = 2010:2024,
  cpi = c(218.1, 224.9, 229.6, 233.0, 236.7, 237.0, 240.0,
          245.1, 251.1, 255.7, 258.8, 271.0, 292.7, 304.7,
          313.7)
) %>%
  mutate(year = as.factor(year))

df <- df %>%
  left_join(yearly_cpi, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(adj_annual_rate = annual_rate * (313.7 / cpi)) %>%
  select(-cpi)

CPI Data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics File Name: Historical CPI-U, August 2025 (XLSX)

EDA

df %>%

  scale_x_log10()

Yeo Johnosn Normalization

  • Identifies good transformation to end up close to a normal distribution.
Code 
yeo_johnson <- powerTransform(df$annual_rate, family = "yjPower")
df$yj_annual_rate <- yjPower(df$annual_rate, yeo_johnson$lambda)

# Reverse Transform Syntax for future reference:
# df$annual_rate_orig <- yjPowerInv(df$annual_rate_yj, lambda)

df %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = yj_annual_rate), bins = 100)

Assessing the Transformation

  • Lambda = 1 would require no transformation to reach normality
  • Lambda = 0 is a log transformation
Code 
print(paste("Lamda: ", round(yeo_johnson$lambda, 4)))
[1] "Lamda:  0.2914"
Code 
summary(yeo_johnson)
yjPower Transformation to Normality 
               Est Power Rounded Pwr Wald Lwr Bnd Wald Upr Bnd
df$annual_rate    0.2914        0.29       0.2892       0.2936

 Likelihood ratio test that transformation parameter is equal to 0
                           LRT df       pval
LR test, lambda = (0) 92849.18  1 < 2.22e-16
Code 
qqnorm(df$yj_annual_rate)
qqline(df$yj_annual_rate, col = "red", lwd = 2)

qqline(log10(df$adj_annual_rate), col = "red", lwd = 2)

Location Distribution

Zipcode Map

Code 
payroll_counts <- df %>%
  distinct(employee_id, zip) %>%
  mutate(zip = as.character(zip)) %>%
  mutate(zip = substr(zip, 1, 5)) %>%
  group_by(zip) %>%
  summarize(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')

ct_zips <- zctas(cb = TRUE, starts_with = "06", year = 2020)
ct_zips <- st_as_sf(ct_zips)
ct_map_data <- ct_zips %>%
  left_join(payroll_counts, by = c("ZCTA5CE20" = "zip"))

percent_joined = (sum(ct_map_data$count, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(payroll_counts$count))*100


p1 <- ct_map_data %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(fill = "white", color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_sf(data = ct_map_data %>% filter(!is.na(count)), aes(fill = count)) +
  # scale_fill_continuous(
  #   trans = "log10",
  #   breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x),
  #   labels = trans_format("log10", math_format(10^.x))
  # ) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Employees by Zipcode",
    fill = "Employees"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
